renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Look at her gently while holding a little breath — that looking is the sign. Breathe out slowly, say the holy word, and picture her awake, standing straight like a stick. She has risen from the base of your body into the middle road. That rising is done; now comes the waking.

The waking climbs through stations: the belly, the heart, the throat, the roof of the mouth, the brows, and the door at the top of the head. Wake each one and rise fast to the place that needs nothing to stand on.

Then she rests in wheels within wheels — soft as a petal, bright, flowing, calm as the sky. The wheel has twelve names: sweetness, crest, and more. She pierces each wheel in turn and rests in every one. That rest is the best thing.
Your body will answer: first the heart shakes, then the head spins, then every limb turns in its joints and the heart churns. That is what true knowing does in the body.

renders.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms.

paragraphs.text: Soft gaze, light breath-hold — that is the sign. Exhale on purpose, speak the word, see her up and rod-straight. She has moved from base camp to the middle highway. Raising: done. Next: waking.
The climb hits every station — belly, heart, throat, palate roof, brows, skull door. Wake them all and bounce to the place that stands on nothing.
Then wheel-rest: soft petal, blaze, flow, steady sky. Twelve names on the wheel. She pierces each one in order and chills in all of them. Supreme rest, no notes.
Body cam turns on: heart shaking, head spinning, every joint rotating, heart churning. That is true knowing running the hardware.
